fact: The article says earlier government announcements linked newborn registration to the planned Unique Personal Identifier (UPI), without dates or detail.

PS Belio Kipsang said on 6 October 2026 that rolling out e-notification to SHA-contracted hospitals by December 2026 would enable children to receive a Unique Personal Identifier (UPI), intended as a common identifier across government systems.

The Interior Secretary says the coming system will give every Kenyan registered at birth a Unique Personal Identifier, serving as the birth certificate number and later the national ID identifier at 18.
Kenya's Civil Registration Services list as next step the adoption of a Unique Personal Identifier, a lifelong identifier assigned at birth.

PS Belio Kipsang said all children will be issued a Unique Personal Identifier (Maisha Number) at birth, kept for life and becoming the national ID card number at 18, through an e-notification system that is built and to be rolled out soon.
The Principal Secretary says the Maisha number is being given to newborns and will run across their lives, used for school, ID, NSSF and NHIF and shown on the death certificate.
